title: Premium Accounting Bulletin: Owner Auto Policy Daily Basis of an Insured-Request Return After a Reinstatement
content:
**Rule.** On a cancellation of an Owner Auto Policy term at the insured's request, the unearned premium is set by the term's recorded reinstatement date and the re-written premium entries booked for a reinstatement. A re-written premium entry is an additional premium entry with reason reinstatement.

| Records on the term | Unearned premium |
|---|---|
| The recorded reinstatement date is on or before the cancellation effective date, and the term carries a re-written premium entry for a reinstatement effective on that date (entries effective on that date taken together) | The daily basis is that entry's amount divided by its days, the remainder having been re-written at that rate. The unearned premium is that daily basis multiplied by the days returned |
| The recorded reinstatement date is after the cancellation effective date, and the term carries the re-written premium entry for that reinstatement | The re-written days never began, so the entry's whole amount is unearned. It is returned in place of a daily basis multiplied by the days returned |
| Otherwise (no recorded reinstatement, or a reinstatement whose re-written premium of 0.00 was not booked) | The daily basis is the term's current full-term rate divided by the term's days. The unearned premium is that daily basis multiplied by the days returned |

The unearned premium this rule gives is the amount any percentage retained then acts on.

**Hypothetical cases.**
- A term was reinstated effective the 12th with a re-written entry of 249.60 covering 96 days. The insured's cancellation takes effect on the 30th with 78 days returned. The daily basis is 2.60, and the unearned premium is 202.80.
- The same term instead cancels on the 9th, before the recorded reinstatement date of the 12th. The whole 249.60 is unearned.
- A term never reinstated, with a current full-term rate of 910.00 over 182 days and 40 days returned, has a daily basis of 5.00 and an unearned premium of 200.00.
